chapter: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
title: After the audition: the men in the rehearsal band, Metcalf and Buster Bailey
summary: Autrey recalls the rehearsal band's players, including Louis Metcalf, Garvin Bushell and Buster Bailey, while mixing it up with the Doc Hyder book he took over from Russell Smith.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well after this brief incident with the Henderson band you must have felt kind of discouraged, didn't you?

Well, not discouraged. I was kind of let down. I would look, I felt that was -- after all, you know, I'm playing Fletcher's music. Who are you? You know. And I walked in and played the book after -- what's-his-name had left, second time. I walked in Doc Hyder's band. He just left. I went in to play --

Russell Smith. Well Russell had just left here, and I walked in there without a rehearsal, and they had been rehearsing all week now. This is a good story. Doc and his band, Garvin Bushell was on, you know (unintelligible) the sax, and Buster Bailey was there playing the alto. Buster was the only one left out of the old band.
Ba ba ba bi di di, let me see can I think of some more. I knew all the guys in the band, because I worked with them before.
Yeah. Yeah. Trombone players, and -- it was a heck of a band, but anyway --
Was Sandy Williams with the band then?

No, Sandy was gone. So oh, I got to mention my man. He was sitting there playing the trumpet, who was very good now, lives in Long Island now. He was on First Avenue there for a long time, with his own band, you know. (Snaps fingers.) Metcalf.

Yeah, Louie Metcalf was up there playing, so I walked in, and man, Louie Metcalf, Herman Autrey, trying to think, who else was trumpet player that was there? Had to be three. Hm. I'll think of that in a minute.
Red Allen was with the band.
No, not then. Oh, this was after Red Allen now.
Now we're talking about this rehearsal still, right, the first --
Yeah, this is rehearsal at his house.
